title: Mitigate sparse-prefix atrophy causing orphaned/duplicated credits in streaming metering
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Incidents and audits have surfaced a recurring class of billing anomalies for long-lived streaming sessions where intermittent client writes and prefix cache eviction produce both orphaned and duplicated token credits. We call this phenomenon 'sparse-prefix atrophy' — when sparse input activity causes the server-side prefix/KV cache to evict or compact entries, subsequent resumed fragments are processed by the metering pipeline with incomplete provenance (missing prefix attribution), resulting in either double-crediting (when a resumed fragment is re-attributed) or orphaned credits that remain unclosed. This ticket scopes a deterministic prevention and reconciliation strategy.
background: Over the past quarter we've seen several customer reports and internal audits: spikes in usage that don't line up with request traces, and retroactive billing corrections. Root cause analysis points to 3 surface issues: 1) prefix cached state is evicted/compressed while session metadata still claims responsibility for future fragments; 2) resume/reconnect paths lack robust idempotency markers for partial fragments; 3) the metering finalizer assumes contiguous fragment ordering and complete suffix lengths, which breaks with sparse client heartbeats and client-side multiplexing. Existing fixes have been ad-hoc (manual backfills, conservative finalization windows) and scale poorly.
proposal: 1) Add a lightweight per-session provenance chain: per-fragment id + prior-fragment-checksum + prefix-length-claimed. Store immutable provenance entries in the metering ledger (compactable but never lost until finalized). 2) Strengthen streaming handshake: clients must include a resume token and last-acknowledged-fragment-id; server returns a canonical resume point. 3) Make finalization idempotent and transactionally atomic: finalizer must cross-check provenance chain before marking credits as settled. 4) Provide a reconciliation worker that replays provenance chains for sessions flagged with non-monotonic offsets and emits corrective ledger entries rather than manual refunds. 5) Add detection rules and dashboards for 'sparse-prefix atrophy' patterns to auto-alert SRE/CS and optionally auto-start reconciliation for low-cost accounts.
tradeoffs: - Pros: deterministic accounting, fewer manual audits, reduces customer-facing billing corrections. - Cons: modest extra storage for short-lived provenance entries, increased write amplification in the metering ledger, implementation complexity across streaming paths (HTTP chunked, WebSocket, gRPC streams). We will mitigate storage cost with TTL-based compaction once session finalized. Performance impact is expected to be <1% P90 tail due to quick provenance writes; we will instrument and can gate behind runtime flag for rollout.
tasks: Design metering provenance schema and compact representation (binary fragment-id + 32-bit checksum + claimed-prefix-length)
Implement resume-aware streaming handshake across HTTP streaming and WebSocket paths
Modify metering finalizer to be idempotent: cross-check provenance chain and compute delta credits
Add reconciliation worker: replay provenance chains to synthesize corrective ledger entries
Add telemetry: detection rule, anomaly dashboard, and per-session trace link in console
E2E tests: simulate intermittent writes, evictions, and reconnects to verify no double-credit or orphaned credits
Load test to validate <1% P90 impact and storage compaction behaviour
Docs + public changelog entry describing billing determinism improvements
acceptance_criteria: No duplicate credits across 1000 simulated sparse-session replays in the E2E test harness
Reconciliation worker can correct historical sessions without issuing unilateral refunds (creates corrective ledger entries and ties to original session trace)
Metric: percent_billing_corrections_generated_by_manual_audit decreases by >=80% in canary region
Latency P90 for streaming request paths increases by <1% after enabling provenance writes
Storage overhead for provenance entries in steady-state <3% of metering ledger volume after compaction TTL
test_plan: Unit tests for provenance serializer/deserializer with edge cases: zero-length prefixes, overlapping fragments, out-of-order fragments
Integration: simulate client that sends heartbeats and sparse payloads, restart server mid-session, validate final ledger state matches expected token counts
Chaos test: evict prefix cache mid-session and trigger reconciliation worker to validate corrective path
Performance: 1M small-fragment stream session benchmark comparing baseline and feature flag on
Regression: run full metering audit harness that validates end-to-end token tallies for mixed HTTP/WebSocket traffic
rollout_notes: Canary region: enable for 10% of traffic with reconciliation worker in dry-run mode (emit suggested corrections but do not write ledger entries)
If dry-run metrics look good, flip reconciliation to active and expand traffic incrementally to 50% then 100%
Monitor percent_billing_corrections_generated_by_manual_audit and stream_credit_delta histogram closely for regressions
Have rollback plan to disable feature flag and run a one-time backfill to revert any provisional ledger rows generated during canary
